# Technology Training for Accessibility

> **Purpose:** Find practical accessibility technology training that can be downloaded directly and used without signing in.

## Introduction

This directory contains **822 free audio and video presentations** about using accessible technology. It is designed for efficient keyboard and screen-reader navigation. Topic categories are H2 headings, and each presentation is an H3 heading. The presentation title is the download link. Activating that title should open or download the AV file itself rather than send you to a watch page, registration page, or sign-in screen.

### Selection and Quality Standards

Entries were kept only when the final review found a reliable, public, direct link to an audio or video file and the presentation had a substantive training purpose. Tutorials, demonstrations, workshops, instructional question-and-answer sessions, and similar practical material qualify. Interviews, advocacy discussions, convention coverage, personal stories, employment discussions, announcements, and general technology commentary were excluded unless they clearly teach how to use accessible technology. Missing metadata was left blank rather than guessed.

Direct-download links were checked without credentials. Redirects could be followed during verification, but the published H3 link keeps the original stable download address rather than a temporary signed CDN address. This matters because temporary redirect URLs can expire.

### Organization

Presentations are grouped by topic at H2 and alphabetized by title within each topic. `Miscellaneous`, when needed, comes last. The year appears in parentheses after each title so readers can quickly judge currency. Metadata fields are alphabetized. `Length` gives approximate listening time rounded to the nearest minute, using forms such as `7 min`, `1 hour 3 min`, and `2 hours 49 min`. Descriptions, when available, are one concise paragraph in plain language; promotional copy, greetings, contact details, and transcript boilerplate have been removed.

Five appendixes provide alternate ways to browse the same presentations: by year, website, presenter, series, and title. Appendix links point back to the main presentation entries rather than duplicating their metadata.

### Sources and Final Preparation

The initial release retains material from these sources: AppleVis (501), BlindAbilities (197), Federal (71), AccessibleWorld (24), Mosen (16), ACB (13). Source labels link to the relevant source pages when that metadata was available. The final preparation combined earlier source-specific directories, removed duplicates and off-topic material, verified direct AV downloads, added listening times where they could be measured reliably, shortened descriptions, normalized metadata, rebuilt internal anchors, and synchronized the table of contents with the H2 structure.

Of the 822 presentations, **812 include a Length field** and **811 include a Description**. Some entries have less metadata because the source did not provide it reliably. That is intentional: incomplete metadata is preferable to false metadata.

### Using This Directory

Navigate by H2 to move among topics and appendixes, or by H3 to move directly among presentations. Activate an H3 title to access the AV file. Use the source link in an entry when you want the publisher's context or related material. Because accessibility software and training links change over time, older presentations may still be useful even when interfaces have changed.

### [Capti Narrator for iOS: Listen to Everything That You Want to Read (2016)](https://www.applevis.com/sites/default/files/podcasts/AppleVisPodcast990.mp3) {#presentation-capti-narrator-for-ios-listen-to-everything-that-you-want-to-read-2016}

**Description:** In this podcast, Thomas Domville gives us a walk-through and demonstration of Capti Narrator, a free iOS app that will convert nearly any text content to audiobooks. Capti supports multiple file types, including PDF, DOC, PPT, EPUB and RTF files, with support for adding content from browsers, GoogleDrive, Dropbox, Bookshare, or Gutenberg.

**Length:** 36 min

**Source:** [AppleVis](https://www.applevis.com/podcasts/capti-narrator-ios-listen-everything-you-want-read)

### [How to Unlock Your iPhone with Your Apple Watch When Wearing a Mask (2021)](https://www.applevis.com/sites/default/files/podcasts/AppleVisPodcast1396.mp3) {#presentation-how-to-unlock-your-iphone-with-your-apple-watch-when-wearing-a-mask-2021}

**Description:** In this podcast, Thomas Domville showcases the new "Unlock with Apple Watch"" feature introduced in iOS 14.5 and watchOS 7.4 that allows the iPhone to use an unlocked and authenticated Apple Watch as a secondary authentication method; making it easier to unlock an iPhone when you're wearing a mask. **Description:** Learning assistive technology isn't just about memorizing shortcuts---it's about building skills that open doors to school, work, and everyday life.
